name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.126.0 — Soft reviewer findings are now advisory: verdict.js's disposition pool holds only hard survivors plus leg findings, so a soft-only reviewer return derives CLEAN with zero dispositions instead of demanding a fix/waive/reject cycle, and the review row carries the soft count as an eighth findings key. FINDINGS keeps exactly one meaning, a dispatched fix that has not landed. The review driver self-dispositions an empty hard pool straight to CLOSE with no DISPOSITIONS mark required, prints soft survivors once under an advisory block that is never routed to the disposer, and --mark dispositions --file now derives the waived/rejected/fix-dispatched tallies from the disposer return itself, with the count flags becoming an optional cross-check rather than a hand-typed requirement. reviewer.md's severity calibration drops the medium level: hard blocks CLEAN until dispositioned, soft is advisory. 7.125.0 — chrome-harness.js's serve(dir, port = 0) asks design-atlas.js's --port 0 for an OS-chosen port instead of deriving one from process.pid, so two concurrent atlas test runs can never collide on a shared port; ready rejects on any first stdout line other than its own serving banner (naming the verb and the held port) instead of treating a sibling run's already serving line as its own readiness, stop() attaches its exit listener before SIGTERM so a cleanup on an already-exited child resolves instead of waiting forever on a listener attached after the event, and withDeadline/withChrome bound every DevTools send and navigate's load wait with a named per-call deadline. design-atlas.js's serve --port 0 now prints the bound port (server.address().port) in its banner instead of the literal 0 it was asked for. 7.124.0 — review-legs.js sets SPEC_REVIEW_BASE in every leg subprocess's environment so a host check running inside the gate or suite leg can judge against the base this review is actually judging rather than a merge-base it re-derives from branch topology (which collapses onto the wrong commit once a branch has merged); plugin-bump.js resolveBase() honors it as a 40-hex-only candidate ahead of main/origin-main. replay.js's --record cross-checks a baseline-red or new pristine-red --legs claim against the cited review run's one CLEAN ledger row instead of trusting the claim on shape alone, and refuses one that row contradicts. replay.md's step 7 rung 3 now resolves a still-red pristine-baseline verification deterministically: a second still-red re-run with the same first failing line records setup-failed with pristine-red:<leg> and stops with its manifests retained, instead of asking the user a question the evidence cannot answer; a different or green result still falls through to the question seam.
